    <span>SFT Methods</span>

  <h3>Data Difficulty and the Generalization--Extrapolation Tradeoff in LLM Fine-Tuning</h3>
  <p>This paper systematically studies difficulty-based data selection for supervised fine-tuning and shows that no single difficulty level is universally optimal. It explains the data-size-dependent optimum through a tradeoff between in-distribution generalization and extrapolation, with the best difficulty shifting toward harder examples as the data budget grows.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

</article>

  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.04</span>
    <span>SFT Methods</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability</h3>
  <p>This paper challenges the common claim that supervised fine-tuning (SFT) only memorizes while RL generalizes, finding cross-domain generalization from reasoning SFT with long chain-of-thought supervision depends jointly on optimization dynamics, training data, and base model capability.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">

<article class="paper-card" id="profit-leveraging-high-value-signals-in-sft-via-probability-guided-token-selection">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.01</span>
    <span>SFT Methods</span>
  </div>
  <h3>ProFit: Leveraging High-Value Signals in SFT via Probability-Guided Token Selection</h3>
  <p>This paper presents ProFit, a supervised fine-tuning method that mitigates single-reference overfitting by using token probability as a proxy for semantic importance and masking low-probability tokens. The approach focuses learning on core logical content and improves reasoning and math performance over standard SFT baselines.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09195" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="beft-bias-efficient-fine-tuning-of-language-models-in-low-data-regimes">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2025.09</span>
    <span>SFT Methods</span>
  </div>
  <h3>BEFT: Bias-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models in Low-Data Regimes</h3>
  <p>This paper studies which attention-projection bias terms to fine-tune in low-data settings and finds that directly tuning the value bias generally outperforms tuning query or key biases. The result holds across encoder-only and decoder-only language models up to 6.7B parameters, including bias-free models augmented with a value bias.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15974" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
